heroHeadline: ICC Orders Taliban Case Split From Afghanistan Probe Covering US Nationals — Significant Jurisdictional Ruling Creates Distinct Docket for Taliban Accountability
heroSubtitle: July 16, 2026 is Day 9,048 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 141 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. Pakistan's security forces foiled a suicide VBIED attack on a military post near Wana, South Waziristan today, killing 4 militants. The 33-day cross-border strike pause noted through June 7 ended June 10, when Pakistan struck Khost, Kunar, and Paktika in response to a June 9 TTP attack on an FC post in Musa Dara that killed 6 personnel — Pakistan claims 26 militants killed, Taliban says 13 civilians died including 11 children. A June 27 Jamaat-ul-Ahrar VBIED and gun attack on a Rangers camp in Karachi, killing 3, triggered Pakistan's largest retaliatory strikes since the pause: on the night of June 28-29, strikes on Chamkani (Paktia), Gyan (Paktika), and Marawara (Kunar) left at least 28 civilians dead and 49 injured according to UNAMA, with Taliban officials and NPR citing a higher toll of 36 killed and roughly 160 wounded — one of the conflict's deadliest single strike episodes. On July 1, Taliban forces launched their first-ever direct drone strikes onto Pakistani territory, targeting an alleged ISIS-K site in Saranan, Balochistan; Pakistan says it intercepted all four drones — a historic escalation beyond artillery exchanges and diplomatic protest. A wave of TTP and Baloch-militant attacks across Balochistan July 4-7 (Hanna Urak in Quetta, and a Mangi Dam police post attack in Ziarat that killed 9 officers) prompted Pakistan to launch Operation Shaban on July 5. On the diplomatic and humanitarian track: the UN Security Council unanimously renewed UNAMA's mandate for a full year via Resolution 2822 on June 16; Paigard News Agency director Jawid Niazi was released July 6 after two months in Taliban intelligence custody, though press-freedom groups say other journalists remain detained; Pakistan's deportation deadline for undocumented Afghans expired July 10, triggering mass-arrest orders and a surge of returnees; and OCHA warned July 14 that more than 10.7 million Afghan women and girls need humanitarian assistance, with HRW publishing a July 15 report raising alarm over civilian casualties from Pakistan's strikes. No formal ceasefire or Urumqi Round 2 meeting has been confirmed — the conflict remains in active escalation.
